detail.longDescription:
I would like to build a progress bar for a multipage REDCap survey that uses javascript to draw the current page number and total number of pages values so I can calculate the percent for each page and plug it into a html element. We only have 1 or 2 questions per page, so the total number of pages displayed with the out-of-the-box "Page X of Y" element makes the survey feel longer than it really is and was discouraging to our pilot testers. I want to avoid hard-coding the current Y value into the calculation 1) in case the page count changes before the survey moves to production and 2) I'd like some generic code I can easily port to other projects. Using "Inspect" reveals that the progress element is

with a span of already-calculated text, e.g. "Page 2 of 20.". Using "View Page Source", I was able to find the input name for the current survey page number and pull it with script: let pageNum = document.querySelector("input[name='__page__']").value; (for that particular page = 2). I can't seem to find where REDCap stores the value for total number of pages (in this case, 20).
